sources.title: Cloudflare incident on February 6, 2025
sources.verified_fact: Cloudflare reports that a product disablement action taken during abuse remediation inadvertently disabled the production R2 Gateway service and caused all R2 operations to fail during the primary incident window.
sources.defensive_abstraction: A service-management action against a critical shared dependency remains subject to an independent critical-service predicate.
sources.limitations: FerrumOS fixtures do not reproduce Cloudflare tooling, R2 architecture, abuse remediation, customer data, or incident impact.

sources.title: Outage post-mortem
sources.verified_fact: Dropbox reports that a subtle upgrade-script bug caused a reinstall command to run on a small number of active database machines, including some master-replica pairs.
sources.defensive_abstraction: Remote maintenance commands that can destroy critical persistent state require local target-state verification before execution.
sources.limitations: The fixture does not reproduce Dropbox databases, operating-system installation, replication, backups, or recovery.

sources.title: Google Cloud incident report: November 16, 2021
sources.verified_fact: Google reports that a race in a configuration pipeline pushed a corrupted configuration to Google Cloud Load Balancing after existing validation failed to reject its actual error form.
sources.defensive_abstraction: Configuration writes to protected live state require local invariant checks even when an upstream validation pipeline has approved them.
sources.limitations: FerrumOS does not model GCLB, Google configuration pipelines, customer rules, fleet propagation, or outage impact.

sources.title: February service disruptions post-incident analysis
sources.verified_fact: GitHub reports that unexpected database load and an unintended configuration issue led to resource contention, including a process-manager interaction that reduced an intended file limit.
sources.defensive_abstraction: Repeated capacity-affecting operations are evaluated against absolute occupancy rather than only action-local deltas.
sources.limitations: The fixture does not reproduce GitHub databases, ProxySQL, file descriptors, process managers, traffic, or service impact.

claim_boundary: These sources are held out from v3.1 threshold selection by an audited file-open guard.
The v3 final scenario catalog is opened development data for v3.1 and is not reused as final evidence.
The v3.1 final benchmark is source-held-out, not an unseen-action or unseen-hazard-family claim.
Every benchmark observation is deterministic software simulation with no production, human, or physical execution evidence.
The catalog contains defensive summaries only and excludes exploit instructions, credentials, and payloads.
